title: Generation of $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ by extensions by zero of lisse sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Let $\mathcal G$ be the class of
objects $a_!L[n]$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, with $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ a locally
closed immersion, $L$ a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Every
$K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is obtained from objects of $\mathcal G$ by finitely many cones: there is
a finite sequence $K_1,\dots,K_N=K$ such that each $K_r$ is in $\mathcal G$ or is isomorphic to
the cone of a morphism between earlier members (up to shift). Conversely every such object
lies in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal T$ be the class of objects admitting the finite construction in the statement. Its starting class contains $0$: take $a=\mathrm{id}_X$ and the locally free module of rank zero. Finite witnesses can be concatenated, so a cone of a morphism between two already constructed objects can be appended after their two witnesses. The class is closed under isomorphism: if $B$ has been constructed and $B'\simeq B$, append $B'$ as a cone of $0\to B$, whose cone is $B$ by the mapping-cone formula. It is closed under shifts: shift each entry of a finite witness; the generators remain generators. Three rotations of a cone triangle with vertices $A,B,C$ give a distinguished triangle with vertices $A[1],B[1],C[1]$ and signed shifted arrows. Thus $C[1]$ is again a cone of a morphism between the shifted earlier objects; no removal of all three signs is asserted. Three inverse rotations give the same assertion for $[-1]$, and iteration handles every integer shift. These observations prove closure directly for finite witnesses, without taking an infinite closure or adding direct summands.

proof.text: We first prove the converse. Factor $a=i\circ u$ through the scheme-theoretic closure $Z$ of $S$, where $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ is open and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is closed; by [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], $a_!=i_*u_!$ is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] first on $Z$ and then on $X$, with the coefficient sheaves identified by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Its formulas give $(a_!L)|_S\simeq L$, $(a_!L)|_{Z\setminus S}=0$, and $(a_!L)|_{X\setminus Z}=0$. Here are the quasi-compactness checks for both applications. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open $W$ of $X$ is quasi-compact. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z$ has the topology of a closed subset of $X$. Every open $V$ of $Z$ is $Z\cap W$ for an open $W$ of $X$, hence is closed in the quasi-compact space $W$ and is quasi-compact: add $W\setminus V$ to any open cover of $V$ to extract a finite subcover. The inverse image of each affine open under either complementary open immersion is an open of its ambient space $X$ or $Z$, so is quasi-compact by these observations. Thus both complementary open immersions are quasi-compact morphisms, exactly as the ringed open-closed node requires. The three locally closed pieces $S$, $Z\setminus S$, $X\setminus Z$, omitting empty pieces, form a finite constructible stratification. On its pieces the restrictions are lisse, including the zero module of rank zero. Thus the constructibility criterion in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] gives $a_!L\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$; [sk-def-sfb-constructible] gives $a_!L[n]\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$. Finally [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated] and induction on the length of any witness put every object of $\mathcal T$ in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$.

Let $F\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$. The constructibility criterion of [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] supplies a finite stratification adapted to $F$. Refine and order it by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1); part (2) ensures that the restrictions of $F$ are still lisse on the refined strata. Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration] with this ordered adapted stratification. It supplies $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$, and identifies $F_k/F_{k-1}$ with $A_k=a_{k!}L_k$, where $L_k=F|_{S_k}$ is lisse. Consequently each $0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to A_k\to0$ is short exact in the ambient abelian category of $\Lambda_X$-modules.

source.place: Single sheaves: the finite filtration, with the existence and ordering of an adapted stratification made explicit

proof.text: Regard the short exact sequence in step 3 as a degree-zero short exact sequence of complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] it gives a distinguished triangle $F_{k-1}\to F_k\to A_k\xrightarrow{\delta_k}F_{k-1}[1]$. Inverse rotation, using [def-weil-triangulated-category], gives $A_k[-1]\xrightarrow{-\delta_k[-1]}F_{k-1}\to F_k\to A_k$. Thus $F_k$ is a cone of a morphism from the generator $A_k[-1]$ to the previously constructed $F_{k-1}$. Start with $F_0=0$ from step 1 and induct on $k=1,\ldots,m$, appending the generator and then this cone at each stage. This is a finite witness for $F=F_m$. Shifting the witness, as in step 1, gives one for every $F[n]$. If $F=0$, the witness consisting of $0$ already suffices.

proof.text: For $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ choose a representing complex $C$ and integers $a\le b$ with $H^q(C)=0$ outside $[a,b]$; this boundedness and the constructibility of every $H^q(C)$ are exactly [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Put $T_q=\tau_{\le q}C$ in the derived category. The formulas in [def-kun-truncations] give $H^r(T_q)=H^r(C)$ for $r\le q$ and zero otherwise: below $q$ the kernel and image are unchanged, at $q$ their quotient is $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$, and above $q$ every term vanishes. Hence $T_{a-1}$ is acyclic and $T_b\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies $T_{a-1}\simeq0$ and $T_b\simeq K$. For each $q=a,\ldots,b$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] gives $T_{q-1}\to T_q\to H^q(C)[-q]\xrightarrow{\partial_q}T_{q-1}[1]$. Inverse rotation gives $H^q(C)[-q-1]\xrightarrow{-\partial_q[-1]}T_{q-1}\to T_q\to H^q(C)[-q]$. By steps 3–4 its first term has a finite witness. Starting with the witness for $T_{a-1}\simeq0$, concatenate that witness and the witness for the first term, and append $T_q$ as their cone. Induction through the finite interval $[a,b]$ constructs $T_b$, and the isomorphism closure proved in step 1 constructs $K$ itself. Vanishing cohomology degrees cause no exception, since their first term is zero. If all cohomology vanishes, $0\to C$ is already a quasi-isomorphism and the zero case of step 1 applies. Together with step 2 this proves both directions.
